pairs.subject: job-coordination
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/storage.rs:1445 Boot recovery selects every running row and sends it through fail(), so a job heartbeated one second ago is requeued or failed with no adopt path for a live sibling.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/storage.rs:1412 Status is one enum and unknown strings fail parse, but retry is a separate UPDATE that leaves failed/cancelled and nulls error, with no actor.

crates/core/src/storage.rs:1523 Heartbeat extends heartbeat_at only while status is running and attempts match, and returns whether the write landed; reap_stale treats an old heartbeat as death. No holder column; attempts is the fence.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:1520 The queue has a renewal write, so the case where no timeout is defensible because the holder cannot renew does not hold.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:3184 Checkpoint replace is attempt-fenced total state, but an unreadable blob is returned as None, so a torn or foreign snapshot is indistinguishable from no position.

crates/core/src/storage.rs:805 Claim writes running on the job row before the worker runs the effect, so recovery can tell dispatched from never-started. Re-run policy is the global attempt ladder, not a per-step field.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:774 The claim, including target exclusion, is one statement. A crash inside fail() after the read leaves the row running, which the reaper can verdict again.

crates/core/src/storage.rs:1445 The sweep condition is status alone. jobs.rs the_boot_sweep_issues_the_same_verdict_the_reaper_does requeues a row whose heartbeat is 1s old. Queued rows are left; there is no adopt.

crates/core/src/storage.rs:1258 JOB_COLUMNS omits heartbeat_at, and oldest-running age is started_at, so a long live job and a dead one are the same gauge. Status rollups do keep absent statuses absent.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:715 Enqueue writes params, budget_usd, max_attempts and app onto the row. set_schedule_budget updates only the schedule. No policy-version or validity floor on the job.

pairs.registryProposal: terminal-state-recovery requires the boot sweep to be time-bounded, while no-wall-clock forbids a wall-clock budget on the call that advances durable rows. Say whether a sweep whose work is its own counted writes may stop between rows on a clock and return a named truncated fact.

pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/routes/jobs.rs:591 Cancel of a running job looks up an in-memory token, and when that registry has no entry the handler reports the job as already terminal.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/routes/jobs.rs:281 List filters unknown status strings through JobStatus::parse and returns 400. Bulk retry only accepts failed or cancelled.
crates/server/src/routes/jobs.rs:484 These handlers do not renew a lease. reset is an operator requeue that relies on the store's attempt fence.
crates/server/src/routes/jobs.rs:591 storage.cancel only updates queued rows. A running job is cancelled by job_cancels. If that map has no token, the 409 text says the job is already terminal.

crates/server/src/routes/jobs.rs:374 GET /jobs/{id} adds an in-memory progress snapshot and leaves the stored job fields unchanged, so lease holder, lease age and next action are not on the operator read after a restart.
crates/server/src/routes/jobs.rs:148 The door validates merged params and budget_usd, then copies both onto EnqueueOptions before enqueue_dedup. Idempotency-Key replays the original job.

pairs.subject: job-coordination
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:1081 A schedule's next firing is projected from durable last_run and last_skipped_at, admission is one closed verdict, and the tick re-reads enabled and budget before enqueue while reaping stale heartbeats.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:1791 Schedule ledger outcomes are checked both ways against SCHEDULE_OUTCOMES. ScheduleAdmission::health is the only spelling of the admission verdict, and admit is the one composer.
crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:154 This loop is the reaper's owner: each completed tick calls reap_once for heartbeat-stale running jobs. Renewal writes and TTL numbers live outside this file.
crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:157 Reclaim on this tick is the heartbeat reaper, which is the expiry family. A death probe is not the mechanism.

crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:1081 The cron reference is the later of durable last_run and last_skipped_at, else created_at. In-memory last_pass only sets the misfire cutoff inside one process; boot uses a two-tick grace.
crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:500 A firing is one enqueue. Overlap looks at the latest job's queued/running status, which is the job row, not a third schedule position.
crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:250 reconcile and decide take the host's instant. They do not carry a budget that promises the pass will finish the admitted work.
crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:592 last_skipped_at, which consumes pending firings, is stamped only after the enqueue, so a failed enqueue cannot eat the run.

crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:153 The same tick that can hold a schedule on an overlapping run also requeues heartbeat-stale running jobs, so an orphan is not left as a permanent overlap block. This file does not issue the boot sweep.
crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:820 scheduler_liveness reads the durable pass heartbeat and treats a missing pass as stale. The decision ledger separates fired, skipped, held and refused.

crates/server/src/scheduler.rs:918 Budget is copied from the live schedule row at enqueue. still_firable refuses a row disabled after the pass snapshot. Params stay the validated snapshot and are what the job is enqueued with.

techniques.evidence: crates/apps/state-tax/src/lib.rs:179 These apps return a result or an error. They do not define or transition job status.
crates/apps/mpsv-vpm/src/lib.rs:1021 Searched heartbeat, lease and reap in these app files. The only reap mention is the job reaper outside the app. No renewal loop here.
crates/apps/mpsv-vpm/src/lib.rs:1020 Lookups are awaited HTTP calls inside run(). Death of the holder is the worker reaper's problem, not a process probe in these apps.

crates/apps/mpsv-vpm/src/lib.rs:1872 Completed IČO records are checkpointed and skipped on resume, but any unexpected shape, including a truncated write, becomes a silent fresh start with no recorded reason.

crates/apps/mpsv-vpm/src/lib.rs:1048 A fetched employer is in the checkpoint and is not fetched again. An in-flight GET that never checkpointed is fetched again; the call is a read, so the two-valued protocol matches an idempotent step.

crates/apps/state-tax/src/lib.rs:334 A short state-tax roster suppresses removal instead of tombstoning the jurisdictions it did not return. smlouvy-dump-watch uses the same floor: a partial parse must not snapshot-delete.
crates/apps/state-tax/src/lib.rs:340 An empty answer fails the app run. These files do not sweep orphaned job rows.
